newsitem.title: JAPAN: Early Asia, futures rise put cash Brent in contango.
newsitem.headline: Early Asia, futures rise put cash Brent in contango.

text.p: Crude oil prices in early Asia on Monday rose in response to the heavy 82 cent gain in the NYMEX June WTI contract on Friday, traders said.
Quiet physical markets saw June cash Brent notionally assessed at $20.15/$20.25 per barrel in early Tokyo trade, with intermonth spreads indicating slight premiums through to August/September.
"Wet trade has been dead, so the contango looks driven by the futures markets' gains," said one trader.
July Brent was assessed three to five cents higher than June, while August was talked at a similar premium to July.
Friday's NYMEX gains came on the back of a technical buying spree, as the June contract broke through key price levels, signalling a stronger market for analysts charting crude.
The bulls took heart from news Friday that North Sea loadings were expected to fall by about 12.50 million barrels in the shorter month of June due to maintenance programs.

In Asian paper deals, a Singapore trader logged a "butterfly" spread, purchasing a July/August Dubai from a Spanish refiner at 24 cents and selling the paper as an August/September deal to the trading arm of a Malaysian refiner at 18.5 cents, for a 5.5 cent spread.
Asian term buyers of Yemeni crude awaited responses to bids they issued Friday for third-quarter Masila crude prices.
Most bids hovered near the second-quarter level of dated Brent minus 50 cents, traders said.
"The spot premium for Masila is running near 10 to 15 cents, so sellers want to increase third-quarter prices by an equal amount," a trader said.
